key_insight: ReCoSplat combines an autoregressive, feed‑forward Gaussian splatting representation with a render‑and‑compare training strategy to enable robust online novel‑view synthesis from sequential posed or unposed observations, even when camera intrinsics are unknown. This closes the gap between stable training with ground‑truth poses and realistic inference with predicted poses.
problem_solved: Online novel‑view synthesis from sequential, often unposed and low‑quality observations — addressing scalability and the train/test distribution mismatch caused by training with ground‑truth poses but deploying with predicted/unknown poses and intrinsics.
method: Autoregressive feed‑forward Gaussian Splatting: assemble local Gaussians per incoming view (scales better than canonical‑space prediction and supports online updates).

Render‑and‑compare training objective: render predicted assemblies and compare to observations to align training with inference, mitigating distribution mismatch between ground‑truth and predicted poses.
Flexible input handling: supports posed or unposed inputs and operates with or without known camera intrinsics, enabling deployment in streaming/robotic settings.
impact: Makes real‑time, scalable novel‑view synthesis more robust to unposed and imperfect input streams, reducing reliance on accurate camera metadata and enabling practical deployment in robotics, AR/VR and online reconstruction pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: sequential/autoregressive assembly of local Gaussians vs canonical‑space prediction (highlighting scalability).
Render‑and‑compare schematic: predicted render vs observed image with error signal back to Gaussian assembly and pose predictions.
Qualitative comparisons: novel‑view renderings for posed vs unposed inputs and with/without intrinsics.
Quantitative charts: reconstruction quality vs pose noise and inference latency / memory scalability comparison.
paper_title: ReCoSplat: Autoregressive Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting Using Render-and-Compare
paper_authors: Freeman Cheng, Botao Ye, Xueting Li, Junqi You, Fangneng Zhan
